subject: Wellness Policy and Recess Regulation Revision
overview: The subcommittee began a comprehensive overhaul of the district's Wellness Policy (ADF), voting to rescind outdated regulations and adopt model language while planning for specialized sub-policies regarding recess and food allergies.

items.title: Adoption of Model Wellness Policy Language
items.summary: The subcommittee approved a motion to replace the existing antiquated policy language with the current Massachusetts Association of School Committees (MASC) model as a baseline for revisions.

items.title: Rescission of Existing Wellness Regulations
items.summary: Approved the rescission of the current wellness procedures (ADF-R), the inclusion of state law text as policy (ADF-E1), and the outdated policy appendix (ADF-E2).

items.title: Wellness Committee and Implementation
items.summary: The body revised draft language to designate the superintendent and principals as implementation leads and established a wellness committee to meet twice annually.

items.title: Nutrition and Health Education
items.summary: Decided to move specific nutrition guidelines to a future food service sub-policy and adopted concise language regarding the integration of nutrition education into the core curriculum.

items.title: Physical Activity and Disciplinary Consequences
items.summary: Building principals raised concerns about prohibiting the withholding of physical activity as punishment, arguing that brief removals are sometimes necessary for logical consequences or restorative practices.

items.title: Physical Education Requirements and Exemptions
items.summary: The subcommittee removed specific minute requirements from the policy to maintain scheduling flexibility but mandated that any material reduction in total annual PE time must be approved by the School Committee.

items.title: Sub-Policy Organization
items.summary: Members agreed to move detailed regulations for recess and food allergies into dedicated sub-policies to be addressed at future meetings.
